verses.english: Linked Discourses 15.20
2. Chapter Two
Mount Vepulla

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“Mendicants, this transmigration has no known beginning.

verses.pali: Pubbā koṭi na paññāyati avijjānīvaraṇānaṁ sattānaṁ taṇhāsaṁyojanānaṁ sandhāvataṁ saṁsarataṁ.
verses.english: No first point is found of sentient beings roaming and transmigrating, shrouded by ignorance and fettered by craving.

verses.pali: Bhūtapubbaṁ, bhikkhave, imassa vepullassa pabbatassa ‘pācīnavaṁso’tveva samaññā udapādi.
verses.english: Once upon a time, mendicants, this Mount Vepulla was known as Pācīnavaṁsa.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana, bhikkhave, samayena manussānaṁ ‘tivarā’tveva samaññā udapādi.
verses.english: And at that time people were known as Tivaras.

verses.pali: Tivarānaṁ, bhikkhave, manussānaṁ cattārīsa vassasahassāni āyuppamāṇaṁ ahosi.
verses.english: The lifespan of the Tivaras was 40,000 years.

verses.pali: Tivarā, bhikkhave, manussā pācīnavaṁsaṁ pabbataṁ catūhena ārohanti, catūhena orohanti.
verses.english: It took them four days to climb Mount Vepulla, and four days to descend.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana, bhikkhave, samayena kakusandho bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho loke uppanno hoti.
verses.english: At that time Kakusandha, the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha arose in the world.

verses.pali: Kakusandhassa, bhikkhave, bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa vidhurasañjīvaṁ nāma sāvakayugaṁ ahosi aggaṁ bhaddayugaṁ.
verses.english: Kakusandha had a fine pair of chief disciples named Vidhura and Sañjīva.

verses.pali: Passatha, bhikkhave, sā cevimassa pabbatassa samaññā antarahitā, te ca manussā kālaṅkatā, so ca bhagavā parinibbuto.
verses.english: See, mendicants! This mountain’s name has vanished, those people have passed away, and that Buddha has become fully quenched.
So impermanent are conditions,
so unstable are conditions,
so unreliable are conditions.

verses.pali: Yāvañcidaṁ, bhikkhave, alameva sabbasaṅkhāresu nibbindituṁ, alaṁ virajjituṁ, alaṁ vimuccituṁ.
verses.english: This is quite enough for you to become disillusioned, dispassionate, and freed regarding all conditions.

verses.pali: Bhūtapubbaṁ, bhikkhave, imassa vepullassa pabbatassa ‘vaṅkako’tveva samaññā udapādi.
verses.english: Once upon a time this Mount Vepulla was known as Vaṅkaka.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana, bhikkhave, samayena manussānaṁ ‘rohitassā’tveva samaññā udapādi.
verses.english: And at that time people were known as Rohitassas.

verses.pali: Rohitassānaṁ, bhikkhave, manussānaṁ tiṁsavassasahassāni āyuppamāṇaṁ ahosi.
verses.english: The lifespan of the Rohitassas was 30,000 years.

verses.pali: Rohitassā, bhikkhave, manussā vaṅkakaṁ pabbataṁ tīhena ārohanti, tīhena orohanti.
verses.english: It took them three days to climb Mount Vepulla, and three days to descend.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana, bhikkhave, samayena koṇāgamano bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho loke uppanno hoti.
verses.english: At that time Koṇāgamana, the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha arose in the world.

verses.pali: Koṇāgamanassa, bhikkhave, bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa bhiyyosuttaraṁ nāma sāvakayugaṁ ahosi aggaṁ bhaddayugaṁ.
verses.english: Koṇāgamana had a fine pair of chief disciples named Bhiyyosa and Uttara.

verses.pali: Passatha, bhikkhave, sā cevimassa pabbatassa samaññā antarahitā, te ca manussā kālaṅkatā, so ca bhagavā parinibbuto.
verses.english: See, mendicants! This mountain’s name has vanished, those people have passed away, and that Buddha has become fully quenched.
So impermanent are conditions …

verses.pali: Bhūtapubbaṁ, bhikkhave, imassa vepullassa pabbatassa ‘supasso’tveva samaññā udapādi.
verses.english: Once upon a time this Mount Vepulla was known as Supassa.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana, bhikkhave, samayena manussānaṁ ‘suppiyā’tveva samaññā udapādi.
verses.english: And at that time people were known as Suppiyas.

verses.pali: Suppiyānaṁ, bhikkhave, manussānaṁ vīsativassasahassāni āyuppamāṇaṁ ahosi.
verses.english: The lifespan of the Suppiyas was 20,000 years.

verses.pali: Suppiyā, bhikkhave, manussā supassaṁ pabbataṁ dvīhena ārohanti, dvīhena orohanti.
verses.english: It took them two days to climb Mount Vepulla, and two days to descend.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana, bhikkhave, samayena kassapo bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho loke uppanno hoti.
verses.english: At that time Kassapa, the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha arose in the world.

verses.pali: Kassapassa, bhikkhave, bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa tissabhāradvājaṁ nāma sāvakayugaṁ ahosi aggaṁ bhaddayugaṁ.
verses.english: Kassapa had a fine pair of chief disciples named Tissa and Bhāradvāja.

verses.pali: Passatha, bhikkhave, sā cevimassa pabbatassa samaññā antarahitā, te ca manussā kālaṅkatā, so ca bhagavā parinibbuto.
verses.english: See, mendicants! This mountain’s name has vanished, those people have passed away, and that Buddha has become fully quenched.
So impermanent are conditions …

verses.pali: Etarahi kho pana, bhikkhave, imassa vepullassa pabbatassa ‘vepullo’tveva samaññā udapādi.
verses.english: These days this Mount Vepulla is known as Vepulla.

verses.pali: Etarahi kho pana, bhikkhave, imesaṁ manussānaṁ ‘māgadhakā’tveva samaññā udapādi.
verses.english: And these people are known as Magadhans.

verses.pali: Māgadhakānaṁ, bhikkhave, manussānaṁ appakaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ parittaṁ lahukaṁ;
verses.english: The lifespan of the Magadhans is short, brief, and fleeting.

verses.pali: yo ciraṁ jīvati so vassasataṁ appaṁ vā bhiyyo.
verses.english: A long life is a hundred years or a little more.

verses.pali: Māgadhakā, bhikkhave, manussā vepullaṁ pabbataṁ muhuttena ārohanti muhuttena orohanti.
verses.english: It takes the Magadhans an hour to climb Mount Vepulla, and an hour to descend.

verses.pali: Etarahi kho panāhaṁ, bhikkhave, arahaṁ sammāsambuddho loke uppanno.
verses.english: And now I am the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha who has arisen in the world.

verses.pali: Mayhaṁ kho pana, bhikkhave, sāriputtamoggallānaṁ nāma sāvakayugaṁ aggaṁ bhaddayugaṁ.
verses.english: I have a fine pair of chief disciples named Sāriputta and Moggallāna.

verses.pali: Bhavissati, bhikkhave, so samayo yā ayañcevimassa pabbatassa samaññā antaradhāyissati, ime ca manussā kālaṁ karissanti, ahañca parinibbāyissāmi.
verses.english: There will come a time when this mountain’s name will vanish, those people will die, and I will be fully extinguished.
So impermanent are conditions,
so unstable are conditions,
so unreliable are conditions.

verses.pali: Yāvañcidaṁ, bhikkhave, alameva sabbasaṅkhāresu nibbindituṁ, alaṁ virajjituṁ, alaṁ vimuccitun”ti.
verses.english: This is quite enough for you to become disillusioned, dispassionate, and freed regarding all conditions.”
That is what the Buddha said.

verses.pali: Idaṁ vatvāna sugato athāparaṁ etadavoca satthā:
verses.english: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:
“For the Tivaras it was Pācīnavaṁsa,
for the Rohitassas, Vaṅkaka,
Supassa for the Suppiyas,
and Vepulla for the Magadhans.
Oh! Conditions are impermanent,
their nature is to rise and fall;
having arisen, they cease;
their settling is such bliss.”
The Linked Discourses on the unknown beginning are complete.
